result.markdown: --- title: "[vals.fmt_chem()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Format chemical formulas. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-tables/blob/main/great_tables/_formats_vals.py#L1258-L1294){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python vals.fmt_chem(x) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} With string values in a list, we can transform chemical formula notation into properly typeset HTML with subscripted numbers, superscripted charges, reaction arrows, and more. The input text should conform to the chemistry notation described in `fmt_chem()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [X]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of string values to be formatted as chemical formulas. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of formatted values is returned. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#b57f9d9c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from great_tables import vals vals.fmt_chem(["C6H12O6", "H2O", "CH4 + 2 O2 -> CO2 + 2 H2O"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['C6H12O6', 'H2O', 'CH4 + 2 O2 → CO2 + 2 H2O'] ``` ::: :::
